text:
Maya: ok team — need quick alignment on how quota tiers map to pricing plans + burst behavior. Product wants a clear mapping for free/pro/enterprise and exact enforcement semantics before we ship the console UI.
Jon: +1. do we want enforcement per-org or per-api-key by default? big difference for shared keys.
Sophie: prefer per-api-key + org-level guardrail. org-level prevents noisy neighbor but per-key lets customers rotate keys and get accurate usage per client.
Alex: agree. implement primary enforcement on api_key, secondary softcap at org level that triggers notifications and gradual throttling.
Priya: product note: enterprise customers expect predictable SLAs — we shouldn't hard-throttle them during incident windows, prefer graceful degradation and fallback to cheaper model or dedicated pool.
Maya: good call. so mapping rough idea:
- free: strict low baseline rate, small burst, immediate 429 once burst exhausted
- pro: higher sustained rate, larger burst, soft throttles (429 with Retry-After) and a short queuing window
- enterprise: high baseline, burst credits, configurable fallback policies + support for reserved capacity
Jon: proposal for token-bucket params (draft):
```
plans:
  free:
    rate: 1/second
    burst: 300 tokens
  pro:
    rate: 10/second
    burst: 5000 tokens
  enterprise:
    rate: 50/second
    burst: 20000 tokens
```
Note: tokens = billing tokens (not requests); streaming vs non-streaming accounted for per-token.
Sophie: we should distinguish embedding units vs generation tokens. embeddings bill differently and should use separate buckets or multiplier.
Alex: +1. implement two parallel buckets: gen_tokens and embed_units. embedding requests consume embed_units bucket only.
Priya: UX requirements for console: show "current burst credits", an estimated reset time, per-key historical burst consumption, and expected throttling behavior. Also add a simulator so customers can see how a pattern maps to their plan.
Maya: rollout plan: gate under feature-flag quota-enforcement-v2. Canary to 5% orgs for 48h, then 25% for 72h, metrics check, then full rollout with a 7-day grace window where we only warn (no hard 429) for new rules.
Jon: metrics to watch: throttle_rate_by_plan, avg_retries, percent_requests_queued, error_budget_burn. Add alert when throttle_rate > 1% for pro or >0.1% for enterprise.
Sophie: implementation detail: store bucket state in redis with per-key keys and an org-aggregate counter. Keep ops idempotent for multi-replica requests.
Alex: for burst credits persistence we can store a leaky-bucket timestamp + credit balance. simple pseudocode:
```
key = "bucket:${api_key}:gen"
state = get(key)
replenish = floor((now - state.last_ts) * rate)
state.credits = min(state.credits + replenish, burst)
if state.credits >= request_cost: allow and deduct
else: deny or queue
```
Priya: legal/compliance ask: enterprise customers may want KMS-backed tokens and audit of quota changes. add audit log events for plan changes and emergency overrides.
Maya: edge-cases: shared projects that programmatically rotate keys -> org guardrail must sum keys and still protect unit economics. Also large streaming sessions can exhaust burst quickly; consider per-stream cap and per-request max tokens.
Jon: should the free plan allow short high-rate bursts for interactive demos? maybe a slightly bigger burst but smaller sustained rate.
Sophie: yep that's the point of burst: lets short demos succeed. we'll keep free burst=300 but cap single-request tokens to 1500 to avoid runaway long streams.
Alex: what about rate-limiting responses? return 429 with structured body:
```
{
  "error":"rate_limit_exceeded",
  "plan":"pro",
  "retry_after": 12,
  "current_credits": 10
}
```
so SDKs can surface better UX.
Maya: love that. infra-bot: will create a kube feature-flag canary job and a dashboards ticket for the new metrics.
infra-bot: created #deploy job 4421 and dashboard ticket D-987, linked to this thread :white_check_mark:
Priya: next steps: engineering to send a concrete PR for config + rollout RFC. Product will confirm final numbers and add to pricing docs.
Maya: assign owners: Jon -> enforcement infra, Sophie -> API/edge behavior + SDK contract, Alex -> datastore/bucket logic, Priya -> product/pricing signoff. I'll track rollout.
Jon: I'll draft the RFC today.
Sophie: I'll add the SDK error shape to the docs.
Alex: starting a spike on redis sharding impact.
Maya: thanks all. ping me if you need the product spreadsheet with expected plan counts.
Priya: thanks — putting on roadmap item Q2 for console changes.
